title: AI That Pays: Lessons from Revenue Cycle — Nathan Wan, Ensemble Health
talk_summary: A healthcare RCM leader describes using GenAI to draft clinical appeal letters and predict/prevent claim denials upstream, with human clinical experts gating final quality. The transferable core is a human-in-the-loop quality gate on generated artifacts plus measuring outcomes (overturn rate, time reduction) rather than just shipping automation.

takeaways.technique: Expert-gated generation with final human sign-off
takeaways.what_they_do: Off-the-shelf model output was insufficient; they built a custom pipeline and require a clinical expert to approve each generated appeal before submission.
takeaways.numbers: 40% reduction in time; higher overturn rate

takeaways.technique: Outcome-based ROI metric instead of hand-wavy value
takeaways.what_they_do: They track a concrete downstream business metric (denial overturn rate) and time reduction to prove the AI pipeline works, not just generation quality.

takeaways.technique: Fix errors upstream, not at the end of the pipeline
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of only improving the appeal (downstream) process, they use longitudinal data to flag and correct errors before claims are submitted.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most of these denials... just need a way to avoid errors that cause these in the first place

takeaways.technique: Unified multi-format data platform before LLM
takeaways.what_they_do: They invested in a single platform (EIQ) to normalize scattered multi-format data before feeding multimodal LLMs, because raw formats challenge any model.
